items.title: Trump threatens to hit Iran 'hard' after saying ceasefire 'over'
items.description: Donald Trump has flagged the US could hit Iran "hard" in coming hours with fresh strikes, after earlier declaring he believes the ceasefire between the two countries is "over."

items.title: Australians face record high rents as agents see 'inquiries flooding in'
items.description: Rents are soaring in several capital cities as low vacancy rates collide with rising interest rates and population growth.

items.title: 'Shouldn't occur': Change demanded after Telstra outage
items.description: Advocates have demanded changes to how telecommunication companies are regulated and held accountable for outages after Telstra became the latest telco to suffer a large-scale network failure.

items.title: How the Telstra outage impacted these Australians
items.description: Millions have potentially been impacted by the Telstra outage. Here's how it affected Australians doing basic everyday things, from making calls to measuring blood sugar levels.

items.title: Emmy nominations 2026 revealed, with The Pitt and Hacks topping list
items.description: The Pitt takes the lead as the most nominated series for the 78th annual Primetime Emmy Awards, with Hacks in second place.

items.title: Cleary 'silences the critics' as NSW make Origin history with decider win
items.description: NSW has produced a historic performance to win the State of Origin series with a win over Queensland at Lang Park in Brisbane.

items.title: Trump calls Iran 'scum' and Ukraine gets big win on wild day at NATO
items.description: The US President says his country will probably continue to attack Iran and says Ukraine will be given permission to manufacture much-needed Patriot missiles as it fights Russia's full-scale invasion.

items.title: 'Twenty minutes or so': The blunt warning of China's nuclear capability
items.description: Victor Gao, the vice-president of a major Chinese think tank, conducts some sabre-rattling in the wake of China's missile test in the Pacific.

items.title: ABC rejects claims of antisemitic bias ahead of fronting royal commission
items.description: The ABC and SBS will face questioning over complaints of bias and antisemitism when executives appear at the royal commission on Thursday.

items.title: 'Profound injustice': Last woman executed in UK pardoned by King
items.description: The case of Ruth Ellis has gripped Britain for decades and inspired the 1985 film Dance with a Stranger.

items.title: 'Not a handout': Australian theatre calls for government lifeline amid show closures
items.description: As two more major musicals bite the dust, the local theatre industry hopes a live performance incentive modelled on a successful UK scheme will provide salvation.

items.title: World Cup quarterfinals are upon us. Here's what you need to know
items.description: The World Cup has whittled 48 teams down to just eight, with the quarterfinals upon us and the finish line in sight. Find out all you need to know about these monumental matches.

items.title: More than 120 NSW crown prosecutors take rare step over DPP report
items.description: Senior crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC issued the extraordinary statement on behalf of the more than 120 barristers who take on cases for the crown.

items.title: Australian 'alien' arrested after ICE investigation, Trump says
items.description: An Australian woman has been arrested in the United States after an ICE investigation allegedly found she had illegally voted in multiple federal elections.

items.title: Calling all budding storytellers living with disability
items.description: If you are an emerging content maker or journalist with disability and have a story to tell, now is your chance to work with the ABC to tell it.

items.title: TV catchphrase quiz: Guess the show from the famous quote
items.description: Now for the story of 20 famous TV quotes, and the one quiz that had no choice but to keep them all together.

items.title: New varieties set Australian coffee industry up for expansion
items.description: Australians are among the world's biggest coffee drinkers but less than 1 per cent of the coffee consumed nationwide is grown locally. That could be about to change.

items.title: SA confirms second H5 bird flu case, two more suspected in Perth and WA
items.description: South Australia confirms its second H5 bird flu case while Western Australia investigates two more suspected detections, as authorities say the virus has not spread beyond isolated wild birds.

items.title: Native title holders celebrate return of 'special country' in access win
items.description: Traditional owners from the Utopia region north of Alice Springs celebrate the recognition of their native title over an area encompassing more than 4,000 square kilometres.

items.title: RBA chief economist warns of more frequent supply shocks
items.description: The Reserve Bank's Sarah Hunter says global supply shocks appear to be occurring more frequently and the RBA will try to adjust to the new reality.

items.title: Police call for help to handle 'disgusting' Facebook comments
items.description: The WA Police commissioner writes to Meta to ask for assistance with Facebook moderation after a number of derogatory comments are left on social media pages.

items.title: Court told former MP knew lying was 'part and parcel' of visa scheme
items.description: A court hears former Wagga Wagga MP Daryl Maguire knew being dishonest to the Department of Immigration was a component of an alleged fraudulent visa scheme.

items.title: Millions of tiny engineers help to restore health of marine ecosystem in WA
items.description: A restorative mussel farm could improve water quality and biodiversity in Cockburn Sound and the project leaders say there's no need to stop there.

items.title: The faces in the crowd at the Ayatollah's funeral
items.description: The strictly choreographed funeral of Iran's former supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has presented a rare insight into the image Tehran wants to project to the world and the men they see as central to it.

items.title: Quiz: Jump in, we're going on a trip around the world
items.description: Which Mediterranean island was a setting for The Godfather? And what's the capital city of Morocco?
